issues.description: Contradictory register-preservation requirements: the problem statement requires the subroutine set_pixel to preserve all registers except EAX ("Außer dem Register eax dürfen keine anderen Registerinhalte verändert werden"), but the template contains a comment instructing students to save registers they modify "except eax, ebx and esi" (implying EBX and ESI need not be preserved). The provided solution preserves EBX and ESI (push/pop), following the problem statement. This mismatch in expected calling/side-effect conventions can confuse students about which registers they must preserve when implementing set_pixel.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the register-preservation requirement across artifacts. Update the template comment at the indicated location to state the same constraint as the problem statement (i.e., only EAX may be modified; all other registers must be preserved), and ensure the set_pixel stub description and any guidance match this requirement. Alternatively, if the intent was different, update the problem statement to reflect the intended register-saving convention consistently and adjust the solution accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect the pixel value to be loaded into register ECX (problem explicitly: 'mov ecx, [esi]' and the template prints using ECX), but the solution loads the pixel into EAX ('mov eax, [esi]'). This is a cross-artifact mismatch about which register represents the same conceptual entity 'pixel value' and can confuse students mapping the required steps to the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the register usage consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution to load the pixel value into ECX (use 'mov ecx, [esi]') as specified in the problem and expected by the template, or update the template/problem instructions and the printf argument ordering so that the solution's use of EAX is clearly documented and consistent.
